title: Der Anschluss ist weg
desc: Forty seconds, and eight people who do not mind
setting: A platform in Hergiswil, the other train pulling out, and a loudspeaker about to apologise.

options.en: Here you are. And the Halbtax.
options.feedback: Both together. A Halbtax price with no card is not a valid ticket, and that costs a hundred francs.
He will ask for the card next. Handing over both saves the second question.

options.es: Ich habe es am Automaten gekauft.
options.en: I bought it at the machine.
options.feedback: He did not ask where it came from. He asked to see it.

options.en: Yes. When does the next one go?
options.feedback: The practical question, and he will have the answer before the loudspeaker does.
Nobody said it was. Eight other people on that platform missed it too and none of them said a word.

options.en: How long do I have to wait?
options.feedback: Also fine, and it is the same question from the other end.
Short. He has forty more people to get through and he says thank you to every one of them.
It is not. And the announcement is about to apologise for it, which is somehow worse.
Fair. It is usually the platform you are standing on, which is not an accident.

options.en: I will be twenty minutes late.
options.feedback: Four words and the problem is gone. Twenty minutes with a message is nothing; twenty without is a thing.

options.es: Anschluss verpasst. Bin um halb da.
options.en: Missed my connection. I will be there at half past.
options.feedback: Even better. He knows the line and the word Anschluss explains all of it.

options.es: Der Zug hatte Verspätung und dann war der andere Zug schon weg.
options.en: The train was delayed and then the other train had already gone.
options.feedback: All true and four times longer than it needs to be. A long message reads as a big problem.
